title: GMKtec EVO-X3 Mini-PC Review Looking at a 128GB AMD Local AI Box
gist: ServeTheHome's external-hardware look at GMKtec's EVO-X3 mini-PC: an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 box with 128GB soldered LPDDR5X-8000 aimed at local AI development, notable for a rare OCuLink port on a Ryzen AI Max system. The excerpt covers design and I/O only, with criticism of limited ports and 2.5GbE.

themes.theme: Ryzen AI Max local AI boxes

insights.claim: AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ chips have been very well received in mini-PCs because of CPU and iGPU performance plus high-capacity, high-bandwidth LPDDR5X, and developers wanting to run inference locally have been quick to buy them.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Local-AI demand is a real end market for AMD's APU line and its mini-PC partners.
insights.quote: software developers looking to test and run inference locally have been quick to snap up the mini-PCs

insights.claim: The Ryzen AI Max mini-PC market is large and high-margin enough that vendors such as GMKtec are on a second design generation (EVO-X2 last year, EVO-X3 now) within the platform's lifecycle.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Signals sustained OEM investment in AMD's local-AI platform.

insights.claim: The EVO-X3 pairs a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T) with 128GB soldered LPDDR5X-8000 that the iGPU (Radeon 8060S, 40 CUs) can tap, and ships with AI development software preloaded.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Defines the spec point for 128GB-class local inference at mini-PC size.

insights.claim: The EVO-X3's differentiator is an OCuLink port (PCIe Gen4 x4, about 64Gbps), rare on Ryzen AI Max systems, giving more external bandwidth than Thunderbolt 4 for an eGPU or accelerator.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Lets a local-AI box be extended with a discrete GPU, widening its use cases.
insights.locator: GMKtec has opted to route four of the Ryzen SoC's PCIe lanes

insights.claim: OCuLink is limited to four lanes because Ryzen AI Max offers only 16 PCIe Gen4 lanes and the rest are needed elsewhere, and the port is not hot-pluggable.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Platform lane budget caps expansion bandwidth.
insights.locator: With the Ryzen AI Max chips offering only 16 PCIe lanes

insights.claim: Skipping a 10GbE controller in favour of 2.5GbE (Realtek RTL8125BG) is a missed opportunity for an AI-development PC, since newer 10GbE chips became cheap and available this year.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Networking is a weak point for clustering or moving model data on these boxes.
insights.quote: Not including 10GbE is quickly becoming a missed opportunity for AI development-focused PC.
insights.locator: Finally, we have the system's dedicated Ethernet jack

insights.claim: The EVO-X3 has only four USB ports and a single 40Gbps USB-C, fewer than most Ryzen AI Max mini-PCs, so OCuLink and USB-C do heavy lifting for I/O.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Port scarcity is a purchase consideration against competing Ryzen AI Max systems.

insights.claim: The EVO-X3 is an upright 41mm all-metal 'monolith' (the EVO-X2 had a plastic chassis) with a required base, 230W external PSU and ventilation on nearly every side.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Design shift reflects the cooling needs of a high-power APU.
insights.locator: One of the most notable design aspects

insights.claim: The base hides the service screws beneath adhesive rubber feet, so the system is not meant to be opened more than a couple of times.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Minor serviceability negative for upgrade-minded buyers.

insights.claim: GMKtec markets the OCuLink port as a gaming eGPU feature, but the reviewer finds it hard to imagine the system used as anything other than a productivity desktop.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Positioning is AI/productivity rather than gaming.
insights.locator: Surprisingly, GMKtec is aiming the EVO-X3
